routing.reason: Accounts, sessions and per-user task scoping across a small API, a migration and the page; fully specified but security sensitive.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, size M — the ticket is a complete feature with acceptance criteria, not an urgent fix — cost if wrong: a plan gate that slows nothing important
Ruling: skip prd — the ticket is already specific, not a vague epic — cost if wrong: a few open product points surface at the frame step

Ruling: skip architecture — the design fits the existing small layout (db.ts migration, tasks.ts queries, app.ts routes, new users/sessions modules) and the ticket fixes the contracts — cost if wrong: a rework of module boundaries

Ruling: skip ux — the ticket specifies the sign-up/sign-in form and sign-out button, the page is one small file; front reuses existing markup — cost if wrong: a plain form that the visual review flags
Ruling: skip seo — a single private app page, no public content — cost if wrong: none to speak of

Ruling: keep frame (po) at medium effort — to pin down edge cases (case-insensitive usernames, scrypt parameters, legacy tasks with NULL user_id, 404 not 403 for others' tasks, malformed JSON) — cost if wrong: a few edge cases found later in review

Ruling: security review at high effort — authentication, password storage, token handling, access control (IDOR) and input parsing are all touched — cost if wrong: a vulnerability escapes; lowering it would save little

Ruling: no squads — the project declares none, the lead plans the whole ticket; the migration is a new entry appended to db.ts (never edit the shipped one) and the dba review step will cover it — cost if wrong: none
Ruling: budget $2.00 — about 337 lines of code, an M change with a security review and visual review — cost if wrong: the run asks the user for more

first: test/qa.test.ts(85,95): error TS7006: Parameter 'r' implicitly has an 'any' type.

criteria.why: createUser lowercases, validates 3-32 [a-z0-9_], returns 400/409/201 with {id, username}; password <10 gives 'password too short'.
POST /api/sessions returns 201 {token}; same 401 'invalid credentials' for unknown user or wrong password, with a dummy scrypt compare.
All /api/tasks routes call userForToken first and return 401 'authentication required' for missing, malformed or unknown tokens, before the body is read.
All task queries filter on user_id; other users' tasks return the same 404 as missing ones.
DELETE /api/sessions removes the token hash and answers 204; a bad token answers 401.
scrypt with a 16-byte salt and timingSafeEqual; token is randomBytes(32), only its SHA-256 is stored; responses carry no secrets.
The migration adds a nullable user_id and queries filter on user_id = ?, so NULL rows are never returned. A legacy-DB upgrade test covers it.
The page has sign-in and sign-up forms and a sign-out button, and sends the Bearer token on each request. Only the served HTML and JS text is tested.
New accounts.test.ts and qa.test.ts, tasks.test.ts updated to sign in, README documents accounts and auth.

findings.what: Adds changes the ticket did not ask for: a 64 KB body limit with 413, JSON object validation, title validation, a 'done' filter 400, a 1024-character password cap, and a generic 500 handler. The password cap is documented in the README and tested. Several of these change the existing API's behaviour.
Task title validation rejects whitespace-only titles but stores the untrimmed title. It is a behaviour change that the ticket does not require.
A second test file overlaps accounts.test.ts (sign-out, sign-in boundaries and ownership are tested in both). It is redundant and its header comment reads like process noise.

The DELETE /api/sessions handler parses the token and then looks it up again through userForToken(header), so the header is parsed twice. Sessions never expire and there is no rate limiting. The README states both.
Adds CSS unrelated to accounts (focus-visible outline, min-height on buttons and inputs).
The 409 is detected by matching the SQLite error message text, which is brittle. The username UNIQUE constraint is exact, so it does rely on lowercasing, which is done.
The constant-time dummy hash and HttpError class are reasonable but add some complexity. The scryptSync calls block the event loop.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion with sound security: scoped queries, hashed tokens, scrypt and a uniform 401. Tests are thorough, including a legacy-database upgrade. It adds unrequested validation and limits, some CSS, and a redundant second test file, which costs it on scope.
